1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant; learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant - Patanjali Sharma with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. - 3609 of 1994, under Sections - 403, 406, 419, 420,
422, 468, 479, 120B, 352, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station - Kotwali, District - Budaun, during pendency of trial.
3. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, at present:
(i) against FIR lodged on 11.3.1994, the applicant is in confinement (in this case)
since 4.6.2018 ;

sentences.text: (ii) the applicant claims to have cooperated in the investigation.
In any case, he has remained confined for almost five years.
(iii) long criminal history of 26 cases is disclosed.

At the same time, while the applicant was serving sentence in one case under Section 302 IPC, it has been submitted, under orders of the Supreme Court, the applicant has hope of reduction of the sentence, upon completion of ten years of imprisonment.

In that regard,
reference has been made to the order passed by the Supreme Court dated 5.9.2022 in Special Leave to Appeal (Criminal) no. 9942 of 2019.

entities.text: Special Leave to Appeal (Criminal) no. 9942 of 2019
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: As to the other cases cited by way of criminal history barring two cases, applicant has been acquitted in nine cases and exonerated in seven cases at the stage of charge-sheet.
Four being petty offences he has obtained compounding and in three cases, proceedings have been stayed by this Court.
(iv) charge-sheet has already been submitted yet there is no hope of early conclusion of the trial

;
(v) on prima facie basis, only for purpose of grant of bail, it has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant, no ingredient of the offence alleged are made out in the present case.

Inasmuch as undisputedly the applicant had obtained a loan of which repayment was also made for some time, only on account of financial condition of the applicant having deteriorated, the loan could not be repaid in entirety.
In that context, FIR allegations have emerged which are not entirely true.
Last, it has been submitted, the applicant is 77 years of age and has remained in jail in this case for almost five years.

(vi) in any case, no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either tamper with the evidence or delay the trial or intimidate the witness.

4. In view of the above, without expressing any opinion on the final merits of the case, let the applicant involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail, on his furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned, with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressuring the witness, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
( iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
